chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: The Hollywood session songs and musicians
summary: Songs like 'I Dream of Jeannie' and 'Corn Pickin'' made with California musicians including Red Callender and Eddie Beal.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And you were still with the Victor label at this time.
Yes.
"So I Dream of Jeannie" and "Drink To Me" were in keeping with the old tradition.
I'm happy about the whole thing. I don't know. Now it may or may not be significant. Maybe he was happy about the whole thing was over.
And "Corn Pickin' was just a novelty too that we picked up out there somewhere.
And these were made with some musicians out in California. It was a pick-up date.
I see Red Callener's name --
Yeah, Red Callender and Eddie Beal. Ulysses Banks, Oscar Bradley, Lloyd

Reese and Leo Trammel.
As you'll notice, the instrumentation is pretty much the same type of instrumentation that they used with the Kirby group.
Yeah.
I noticed that the first Claude Thornhill big band records were made in September 1940 out in Hollywood.
Yes.
So, maybe that's what he --
That's possible. Yeah, yeah.

I mean, let's face it. Because of his association, and, of course, his work behind me -- the arrangements may have enhanced his prestige; so they began to know who Claude Thornhill was.
He probably went out there and they probably got him -- Because I really don't know what he did.
You don't remember if he worked on a movie score, for instance?

No, I didn't hear that he had, because our relationship was going much estranged by that time. I don't know. He didn't do anything in the movies with me -- you know, like any of the arrangements. They were done by whoever they had in the studio. And this is before Claude got his big band together too. So, he may have been -- You know, I think this is a little bit too early to be thinking in terms of the war, but he might've been drafted and was working in Special Service. He might've been in the Navy at the time and in Special Service and working out there. Because it wasn't until after the war that he actually got a commercial band together and went on the road. But I do know that he was in the service, and he probably was in the service doing some things at that time. That might've been the reason for his being out in California.
(Inaudible).
Yeah.

And so we did this session and that was it.
Okay. Do you --
I have 'I Dream of Jeannie,' and I've had 'Drink To Me Only With Thine Eyes' on tape, of course. But I haven't even heard 'I'm Happy About The Whole Thing' and 'Corn Pickin' in years.
